content: Start by reading TASK.md, then complete the assignment.

content.content:
1	# Task 2: forest of 10,000 instances
2	
3	Build a scene with three.js 0.185.1 (`three` and `@types/three`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A ground plane and exactly 10,000 scattered objects drawn with instancing (not 10,000 separate meshes): 8,000 trees (a trunk and a canopy, each instanced) and 2,000 rocks.
7	2. Placement is deterministic from a fixed seed (same forest every load), no overlaps needed.
8	3. Per-instance colour variation (canopies and rocks do not all share one colour).
9	4. One directional light that casts shadows, and exponential fog.
10	5. The camera slowly orbits the forest and the whole scene is visible.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.
21

content.thinking:
I need to type-declare the global ready flag, then set up the scene parameters: a shadow camera spanning roughly ±70 units, a 2048 shadow map, and an orbiting camera at radius ~110 and height 60. I'm planning tree trunks and canopies as instanced cylinders and cones (8000 each) with per-instance coloring, plus scaled dodecahedron rocks scattered across a 60-radius disc using a square-root distribution for even density.

Working out the forest's scale: with ~11300 m² of area for 10000 trees, density is sparse enough to avoid overlap, so I'll size trees around 3-5 units tall across a 100x100 square with a 140-unit ground plane. I'm tuning the camera (distance 90, height 45, fov 50) and fog density (~0.007 exp2) so visibility falls off naturally by the far edge, and setting up the directional light with shadow camera bounds of ±75 and a 2048 shadow map, plus configuring the renderer canvas at 640x360 with pixel ratio 1.
Checking visibility at that camera distance with the fog settings, the attenuation works out reasonably — around 60% visibility at 118 units, which seems acceptable for the forest scene.

input.summary: I wrote src/main.ts. It builds the forest from three InstancedMesh objects: 8,000 trunks, 8,000 canopies and 2,000 rocks, so 10,000 instances in all. They stand on a 400×400 ground plane. Placement uses a seeded mulberry32 generator, so the forest is the same on every load. Canopies, trunks and rocks each get per-instance colours through `setColorAt`. A single shadow-casting directional light lights the scene, with a hemisphere light as non-shadow fill. Fog is `FogExp2`. The camera orbits slowly at radius 105 and height 55, looking at the centre of the 100×100 forest. It renders in a `requestAnimationFrame` loop and sets `window.__EVAL_READY__` after the first frame. The typecheck passes. I couldn't run `vite build` or view the render here, so I haven't checked how the framing, fog density or shadows look in the browser.
